What is a Builder Buyer Agreement?

A builder buyer agreement (also called an agreement between builder and buyer) is a binding contract outlining terms for purchasing property from a developer. It details the builder buyer agreement process, from booking to possession, including payments, timelines, and specifications.

Under RERA, every builder buyer agreement under RERA must follow standardized norms. The builder buyer agreement format as per RERA ensures fairness, covering everything from plot size to amenities. Key Clauses in a Builder Buyer Agreement You Must Read Before Signing

Not all clauses are created equal. Scrutinize these essentials in any builder buyer agreement to safeguard your rights:

  • Payment Schedule: Specifies installments tied to construction milestones. RERA requires linking payments to verified progress, preventing overpayment before delivery.
  • Possession Date: A firm timeline with penalties for delays (e.g., interest at 10.05% per annum under RERA). Check for force majeure clauses that can't excuse endless postponements.
  • Specifications and Amenities: Details exact carpet area, materials, and promised facilities. Omshakthy Homes ensures these match our plotted developments in Chennai.
  • Price Escalation and Charges: Locks in the total cost, including builder buyer agreement charges. Watch for hidden fees like maintenance or parking.
  • Cancellation and Refund Policy: Outlines forfeiture limits (max 10-20% under RERA) and timelines for full refunds minus processing costs.
  • Dispute Resolution: Prefers arbitration or consumer courts over civil suits.

The supreme court judgement on builder buyer agreement, like the 2019 Pioneer Urban case, reinforces that these clauses must be fair and specific. Always demand the builder buyer agreement format upfront for review.

Red Flag Clauses to Reject Before You Sign

Some developers sneak in unfair terms. Reject these red flags in your builder buyer agreement:

  • Unilateral Amendment Rights: Clauses letting the builder change plans without consent. RERA prohibits this.
  • Excessive Delay Penalties: Only buyer-side fines for late payments, with no reciprocal builder penalties. Insist on symmetry.
  • Arbitrary Price Hikes: Escalation beyond agreed indices or without mutual consent.
  • Indefinite Force Majeure: Broad excuses like "government delays" without time limits.
  • High Forfeiture on Cancellation: Over 10-20% earnest money retention.

A landmark supreme court judgement on builder buyer agreement in 2021 (Experion Developers vs. Sushma Ashok) struck down vague clauses, empowering buyers. If plot developers in chennai push these, walk away—choose transparent ones like Omshakthy Homes.

Checklist: What to Verify Before Signing the Builder Buyer Agreement

Use this quick list for peace of mind:

  • RERA Compliance: Confirm the project is registered on Tamil Nadu RERA portal. Review the builder buyer agreement format as per RERA.
  • Project Documents: Verify approvals, land title, and encumbrance certificate.
  • Registration Details: Understand builder buyer agreement registration process and builder buyer agreement registration fees (about 1% of property value in Tamil Nadu, plus stamp duty).
  • Lawyer Review: Have a legal expert check for ambiguities in the agreement between builder and buyer.
  • Payment Protections: Ensure 70% of funds go to a RERA escrow account.
  • Possession and Handover: Clear terms on delays, with liquidated damages.
  • Warranties: Structural defect coverage for 5+ years.
  • Exit Clauses: Fair refund policy if you back out early.
